title: Impulse Body Text 5
description: One specific form of Assisted Solo is the Pressure exercise. Here, two assistants offer any possible part of their bodies as surfaces for the soloist to resist against. The task for the soloist is to respond with resistance to all the surfaces in contact with her. All parties involved can vary the pressure on those surfaces that create movement. It is a dynamic system relying on interactions between the three dancers.

title: Impulse Title Quote
description: “I like to conceive of movement as impulses. Impulses are starting points initiated without a plan for how the entire movement is going to develop. In this conception of movement, you don’t have an intellectual image of a whole sequence of motion. Instead you expose your body to impulses, you vary and accumulate rules, initiations, directions, connections, tension/release, and you let the solutions emerge.” Thomas Hauert

title: Impulse Body Text 7
description: A still more complex form of Assisted Solo is the Mixed Strategies dance, in which several types of touches and impulses are combined to create a more dynamic dance.  A Mixed Strategies dance may include controlled Pressure interactions, but also impulses where momentum is passed from the assistant to the soloist.  Tension and tension-release are two other parameters that come into the game: letting a force move you, modifying it, or resisting it.

title: Habit Body Text 2
description: Thomas Hauert and Zoo Company have developed an exercise they call the Careful Scientist, which uses a very tight set of rules to complicate the coordination between limbs across the two sides of the body. The ultimate goal of this exercise is to translate the intricate combinations it produces to any joint of the body, including the fingers, toes, and the chain of the spine.

title: Habit Body Text 4
description:
Rules for the Careful Scientist Exercise
The Careful Scientist Exercise consists of a very limited set of four actions in certain joints of the upper body. Usually it is practiced lying on the floor, but it can also be done standing. The goal is to teach the body to execute two of these four movements simultaneously in the left and right arm using the following constraints.

Avoid symmetry and opposites in the two arms to:

1. Execute different actions on the left and right simultaneously.

2. Build up to overlapping timing on the two sides of the body by initially starting and stopping both sides at the same time and then eventually working up to overlapping motion (change the actions in both arms at different times, so that the action in one arm continues while the other changes).

3. Work to add complexity by changing durations and amplitudes for the different movements, trying to separate all these parameters left and right.

4. After practicing the upper body, movements in the legs, hips, and knees can be added for a greater challenge.

title: Tendency Body Text 3
description:
The Story State is derived from Angie Hauser’s ways of moving and giving attention when working with Bebe Miller Company and, in particular, in duet work with Darrell Jones. Bebe highlights the way Angie uses her gaze actively, reading and responding to the environment both real and imagined and to the others in the space.

The Drive State is derived from Darrell Jones’s ways of moving and giving attention when working with Bebe Miller Company and, in particular, in duet work with Angie Hauser. Bebe highlights Darrell’s tendency to use more internal sensing forms of attention, responding through touch and cues caught in the periphery of his vision.

The Risky Weight State can be seen in the two previous states and is derived from Bebe Miller’s movement tendencies. It relates to her interest in “interrupting the inevitable,” which can mean stopping, furthering, or redirecting an action unexpectedly.

title: Memory CallOut Text 3
description:
“We are calling on and opening up to things firing in deep embodied memory. Maybe it is a neurological unconscious score. We say yes to imagining the physical manifestation. We flow and then catch a remembered action before it completes and glides into something that's interesting at that time. Memory is always a fiction, the more we do it the more we remember the remembering.”
----- Angie Hauser

title: Memory CallOut Text 4
description:
"Redux is a choreographic improvisation structure based on recall of existing material. The interplay between what’s remembered, what’s recalled, and what’s new is the basis of Redux.”
----- Bebe Miller

additional_fields.html-content:
"Redux is a choreographic improvisation structure based on recall of existing material. The interplay between what’s remembered, what’s recalled, and what’s new is the basis of Redux.”

title: Memory CallOut Text 5
description:
“We have recognized that the power of the choreographed moment has much to do with the live intentions that are set on various vectors, and with improvisation we are interested in how we (and an audience) might respond to that reality. We are arriving at the level of exquisite detail in repeated actions—but making them new each time.”
----- Bebe Miller

description:
“We often work with furthering and risky weight, where weight (either standing or in floor work) is shifted at the last minute. The feeling is similar to finding that there’s one more step down unexpectedly, or the weight at risk as you step on a banana peel.”
----- Bebe Miller

title: Tendency CallOut Text 3
description:
“The specifics of the body’s action have always been my focus, particularly the dynamic and rhythm of attention in the body: where does the impulse travel, how can that be interrupted and redirected, what’s the change of sensation as it travels, what might it remind you of (which is where context and memory begin), who is doing it to/with whom, can one kind of action be sustained in the presence of another?”
----- Bebe Miller

title: Habit Body Text 1
description: Thomas Hauert’s creative process often begins from an investigation of the workings of the locomotor system and, in particular, the joints, those points of articulation between bones that allow changes in spatial relationship to occur. In this aspect of his work, Thomas is focusing his investigations on the way our joints move, their ranges of motion, and the programmed coordinations between them. He and his dancers work to become aware of habits from daily life or training and to devise tasks to retrain or restrain those habits and expand the palette of possibilities.

title: Impulse Body Text 6
description: In the Loose Impulse strategy, instead of holding, resisting, or applying pressure, the soloist allows all of the imposed forces and directions to combine in her body and then prolongs them, slighting and suspending them while waiting for the next input.

title: Tendency Body Text 1
description: One way that Bebe Miller investigates the thinking body and dancing mind is by heightening and distilling her dancers’ movement tendencies and ways of giving attention into states for improvisation. These states also emerge from Miller’s own tendencies and from the many years of working together as a company. The three states we feature here are Story, Drive, and Risky Weight.

title: Tendency Body Text 4
description:
Story State:
“When I watch Angie, I notice how her focus precedes, follows, and drifts out of sync with the kinetics of the moment, so Angie carries with her an impression of being elsewhere and then suddenly deep inside the present moment. On the inside, from her point of view, she is keeping her weight at risk, actively solving level changes past the expected resolve, or tracing an exterior point and then shifting to a more visceral, torso-centered engagement. On the outside we follow her focus and intelligence, which seems to bring context to what she is doing, a sense that whatever room she is imagining is giving her tangible stories and obstacles to deal with. She may not be imagining anything, but we get to play what that might be.”
----- Bebe Miller

title: Tendency Body Text 5
description:
Drive State:
“Darrell’s own work during the 2000’s (two works with Ralph Lemon, his research on Forsythe’s Improvisation Technologies, and his own choreography) greatly informs the dynamic of what became this Drive State. The physical directives that produce the Drive State are a set of tasks pushed to high velocity. He is tracing the periphery of the room, moving with a repeated rhythm in the lower body, creating opposition between the pelvic and limb gestures, and covering space through recovering his weight. All of it is done at full velocity, however, pushed to a high speed while looking for his physical edge, his exhaustion point.”
----- Bebe Miller

title: Tendency Body Text 2
description: Bebe Miller pays great attention to interesting tendencies and feeds these back to the dancers in rehearsal. For example, she might identify the way Darrell tends to rock his head and pelvis to maintain an internal rhythm or the way Angie often initiates with her focus and creates stops and starts in time that generate a sense of alertness.

title: Impulse Call Out Text 2
description:
“Once momentum is added, the soloist is being pushed and pulled off balance all the time, which constantly changes the situation of the body in relation to the floor. The speed of the interactions between all the motors and other elements involved doesn’t allow for very much conscious control.”
----- Thomas Hauert

title: Verge Original Duet (The Bebe Miller Company, 2001)
description: View the original duet performed as part of an evening length quartet called Verge (2001). This duet serves as the memory resource for all of the Verge Redux improvisations. Compare to the four Redux improvisations and note how the dancers draw from this original material. Dancers: Angie Hauser, Darrell Jones

title: Careful Scientist Demonstration by All Three Dancers
description: Demonstration of the Careful Scientist task, one of many training exercises Thomas Hauert and Zoo Company have designed to challenge habitual patterns of coordination and attention. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

title: Careful Scientist Demonstration
description: Demonstration of the Careful Scientist training exercise. This task uses a very tight set of rules to complicate the coordination between limbs across the two sides of the body and to keep one movement going while another is initiated. In this demo, Thomas builds up to overlapping timing. Dancer: Thomas Hauert

title: Assisted Solo Performances, Mixed Responses
description: Assisted Solo performances in which a soloist receives external impulses from two assistants and uses a mix of different possible responses. Finally, the soloist continues the dance alone, recalling the timing and coordination of the inputs received. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

title: Assisted Solos by All Three Dancers, Loose Impulse
description: Dancers switch roles in this ongoing relay of Loose Impulse Assisted Solos. This strategy adds momentum to the mix and the soloist is letting all the imposed forces and directions combine in the body and is prolonging and suspending them slightly while waiting for the next input. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

title: Mixed Roles Group Form, Performance 1
description: Mixed Roles performance from an early Motion Bank residency with Zoo Company with Samantha van Wissen performing. This more complex Assisted Solo game makes everyone both assistant and soloist, creating a network of reactions and "one body out of many." Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Samantha van Wissen

title: Mixed Roles Group Form, Performance 2
description: The Mixed Roles Group Form is a more complex development of the Assisted Solos approach in which everyone acts as both soloist and assistant at the same time, giving and receiving inputs. Shot in slow-motion. Dancers: Thomas Hauert, Sara Ludi, Mat Voorter

title: Tendency CallOut Text 2
description:
“The two dancers featured in this project (Angie Hauser and Darrell Jones) have the immediacy of their 15-year history as dance partners, along with their inescapable interior landscapes to work with. And Talvin Wilks (Dramaturge) and I have a 15-year history of watching them meet the various situations we’ve built, along with our own agendas that we bring to the table.”
----- Bebe Miller

title: Overview Body Text 1
description: Both Thomas Hauert and Bebe Miller are currently choreographing improvisation for performance and are engaging directly with the nature of human consciousness. When we watch them and their dancers, we are watching them at work. We are witness to the concentration and forms of attention that they bring to the moment and to how they work with their habits, tendencies, impulses, and memories in action.

title: Overview Call Out Text 1
description:
“Performing improvisation and the methods we have devised for rehearsing improvisation all arise from my desire to maximize the creative possibilities of the body in motion and to go beyond the habits inscribed in it.”
----- Thomas Hauert

additional_fields.html-content:

title: Overview Call Out Text 2
description:
“We are generating movement strategies that unfold in ways that are not as feasible in step-by-step choreography, for us. We specify the intentional body-mindset and allow the movement articulation — the dancing — to respond to the frame or strategy.”
----- Bebe Miller

title: Overview Call Out Text 3
description:
“My way of creating movement relies on the richness of human consciousness. In our dancing we explore the interaction between attention, focus, reflexes, conscious command, and sensory feedback.”
----- Thomas Hauert

title: Overview Call Out Text 4
description:
“Over the years I have become more and more interested in articulating the prescriptive: the conditions in which action occurs. Performance improvisation is a process of defining the premise for movement, it is monitoring the swing of attention from the kinetics to the situation.”
----- Bebe Miller

title: Habit Body Text 5
description:
“The body has a tendency to stop one action when starting a new action. With this exercise and others, we are interested in training ourselves to continue a particular task even while our attention is busy initiating another movement, something like juggling.”
----- Thomas Hauert

title: Memory Body Text 2
description:
The Redux structure for improvisation is a way of consciously accessing embodied history or memory by recalling a set dance performed in the past and referencing it to create a new one. This creative process involves several strategies, including:

1. Quoting and resequencing choreographed actions

2. Transposing an action in time, space, shape, body part

3. Changing roles

4. Recalling the choreographed timing and sequence but not exact actions

5. Offering beginnings or endings of actions, waiting, and finding new solutions

6. Echoing the quality of touch from the past in a new action

title: Phrasing Landscape of Movement Tendencies
description: The dancers’ personal recipes for performing are influenced and distilled through the lens of the director. This visualization traces the actions of each dancer’s head and pelvis to create a landscape from their individual choices.

title: Assisted Solo, Mixed Strategies (Motion Capture)
description: The Assisted Solo strategy works to short circuit habitual patterns of coordination by giving a solo dancer several external impulses from assistant dancers. The exercise emphasizes the inputs and actions of the soloist but, as this motion capture data shows, the assistants' motion also reveals interesting patterns. Dancers: Thomas Hauert and Mat Voorter

title: Assisted, Solo Pressure (Motion Capture)
description: In this motion capture data, you are able to see the soloist alone and then watch the results of the input from assistants on the soloist's actions. Assisted Solos are a creative tool and training exercise Zoo Company uses where partners or assistants determine the chain of places where motion can happen in the actions of a soloist. Dancer: Sara Ludi

title: CreditAcknowledgementsPart3
description:
Motion Bank, is a project of The Forsythe Company providing a broad context for research into choreographic practice. The main focus is on the creation of on-line digital scores in collaboration with guest choreographers to be made publicly available via the Motion Bank website.

The results were launched publicly as part of a suite of "score" projects for the Motion Bank initiative of The Forsythe Company on November 28, 2013.

CreditAcknowledgementsPart2
description:
The phrase “the dancing mind and the thinking body” is borrowed with permission from the writing of scholar David Gere in a volume on dance improvisation that he co-edited with Ann Cooper-Albright entitled “Taken by Surprise” (Wesleyan University Press, 2003). Gere’s excellent introduction to the text is one of the best overviews that we have found of the rich mind and body experience that is dance improvisation.

PACT Zollverein Choreographic Center in Essen, Germany provided a valuable research residency for Norah Zuniga-Shaw in December of 2011, which was central to the collaboration with Thomas Hauert.

Additional funding for the Two project was provided by Grants for Research and Creative Activity in the Arts and Humanities, Research Foundation, The Ohio State University.
